description: Audio Database harman/kardon CT-1 ¥ 65,000 (around 1988) Commentary A balanced input / output interface based on the sound quality concept of the Citation series. It converts the normal (unbalanced) output into a balanced output, solves the problem of sound quality degradation caused by ground grounding, and supports the balanced input normally installed in high-end equipment. Between normal input and normal output, the transformer performs as a matching transformer and eliminates unwanted noise that adversely affects sound quality. An absolute phase switch for changing the phase has also been made. The transformer uses a high-quality permalloy core and a five part balanced winding. In addition, it is double-shielded with a permalloy shield case to prevent induction from the outside. It is firmly fixed inside a large shield case with special filler. In addition, we have taken care of the terminals by using ノイトリック's gold-plated canon type for the pin terminals and balance terminals, which are both gold-plated and Teflon insulated. Commentary This speaker system improves the time it takes to reach the listener by improving the line arrangement of the speaker unit. In Reference I, the V-line arrangement is adopted for the unit layout. The woofer unit of the long travel voice coil is placed in the center, and the short travel voice coil is placed outside the center. As a result, the difference in time between the sound coming from each unit and reaching the listener's ear is minimized, and the phase characteristic is improved by shortening the time difference between units. The unit is a 4-speaker configuration with a 27.4 cm polypropylene cone woofer for the low range, a 13.7 cm polypropylene cone squaker for the middle range, and a double ribbon tweeter for the high range. The enclosure has a walnut oil finish.
